title: feat: a session starts from a checked resume packet
headline: A new or compacted session starts from one checked resume packet instead of re-reading every tracking file, and the rule text held back from 1.29.0 lands now that the recall test measures it fairly.
alignment: v1.30.0 is build 4 as planned: the push question steadied, the waiting rule text landed, and the resume packet built, each measured on its own recall run.

items.text: The resume packet: each closeout and compact saves the resume point, open lessons, git state and file hashes in about 2 KB. A session starts with one check that names only what changed; any doubt means the full reading.
items.where: What a session reads before its first edit
items.before: Every tracking file, twice: inlined at start, then read again
items.after: One check, then only the plan and what changed

items.text: The cost rule: before a run that spends money or a shared quota, say what it costs and offer the free option first.

Rule 11: first the packet check, then fresh reads of what it names. The tracking files no longer load at start, so nothing loads twice: 44,288 to 32,963 bytes. Status names old start lines a filled-in project keeps.
The owner's yes is a tap in the choice pop-up quoting the act; typed words only where the tool or model has no pop-up.

Nothing carries to the next build by default: a low or medium finding carries only on the owner's yes, a high or critical never. The rules, the Active Plan template and the sweep guard say it one way.
A test is owed for a change in behaviour; wording, docs and removals owe none.
"Held" has one meaning in the guard texts, and the PR title rule counts the squash suffix.
The recall test is version 9: question 4 asks the push and PR decision only, a new question 14 asks how a yes is asked, and keys 3, 12 and 14 follow the rules above.

verification: Each stage had its own recall run against the released 1.29.0, control 0 each time: stage 1 probe 7 of 8 and 8 of 8; stage 2 median 14 to 13; stage 3 and the final text median 14 to 12.
Every fix that changes behaviour shipped with a test that fails on the code before it: 8 of the 14 packet tests fail on the swept code.
The start load was measured on the kit's templates before and after: 44,288 to 32,963 bytes.

decisions.decision: Question 4 is split, and a new question asks how a yes is asked
decisions.why: Sessions gave the push and PR decision in 12 of 12 saved answers; the key hid two items scorers read two ways. The owner picked the split over dropping them.

decisions.decision: The check shows only what it rebuilds from the files
decisions.why: The review showed a saved packet could carry text, or a second verdict line, to the session. Rebuilding from the files leaves the packet only its hashes and its git line.
Rule 11 exists for a real drift; the owner locked the new words by pop-up before the build.
